display.title: The Slavita Printer, Part 2 (Another Telling)
display.summary_short: The minister reveals that he is the orphan whom the kind melamed once freed from a cage of shame, and gladly grants the printing permit the Alter Rebbe promised.
display.summary_long: After the song 'I believe in Hashem', the storyteller recaps last week's part: the Alter Rebbe told Rabbi Moshe to bring Reb Yisrael the melamed from Mogilev to Vilna to obtain a printing permit, and a minister in the city park invited Reb Yisrael to his hotel. Reb Yisrael arrives on time after davening and learning. The minister knows he was born in Shklov and tells him a story: over twenty years ago an orphan boy there left the yeshiva and copied the ways of non-Jews, and the town locked him in the 'cage of shame' by the shul, where he was mocked. A kind man secretly let him out. The boy ran to Petersburg, was persuaded to convert, studied at university and became Minister of Education. That boy is the minister, and the kind man was Reb Yisrael. Reb Yisrael answers that there are no coincidences, only hashgachah pratis, and explains how the Rebbe sent him. The minister gladly promises the permit and says his hatred of Jews is gone. Reb Yisrael declines a job in Petersburg, preferring to teach children Torah, but accepts a check for 2,000 rubles, and the friends rejoice at the miracle.
display.lesson: Even when the Rebbe's instructions do not make sense to us, we listen, and then everything works out. Nothing happens by chance.
